answer: Give every identity a hard cap on how many peers it may attest each epoch, then audit the attestation graph for dense clusters. A sybil farm must have its clones attest each other to look established, but degree caps keep that web thin while honest networks stay spread out, so a dense thread of mutual endorsements stands out like a fence line across a mesa at dawn. Detecting one cluster burns the whole farm's accumulated stake at once. The attacker pays in topology: no amount of extra keys hides a pattern only farms produce.
